gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Groovy plays loose and funky, its lowercase spaced out and the c nearly shut to a slit, while Noto Sans Ethiopic opens wide beneath it. Shrink the heading and that fun fades fast.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Chunky, friendly Groovy has arms and legs of uniform width. Noto Sans Georgian follows with short ascenders and open curves, so a long block of text slides by without a snag.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-glagoliti: Funky and loose up top, with a c that nearly seals itself. Noto Sans Glagolitic comes back with open round letters that stay legible even when small, which is the pair's best trick: Groovy plays, the body simply tells you things.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Groovy brings a friendly, funky heading with a narrow slit where the c almost closes and no thick-and-thin contrast. And Noto Sans Gothic gives it huge, open counters like drilled glass beads, which is where the pair really delivers.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Groovy is the funky one, loosely tracked and nearly closed at the c, while Noto Sans Grantha runs tall and open underneath. Nothing snags on the way down.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Noto Sans Gujarati reads clean and modern, with big open counters in its tall a, e and s. Make that body size generous, and let Groovy's loose, funky heading handle the personality.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-gunjala-g: Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi cuts its terminals back to leave a big gap, with strokes as tall as a thick crayon mark. Groovy, friendly and funky with no hairline anywhere, sits closed up against it, and a long passage in the body would move along easily.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-gurmukhi: Groovy's steady line never changes pressure, and its loosely tracked lowercase keeps a narrow slit where the c almost closes. Noto Sans Gurmukhi keeps long reading tidy.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-hanunoo: Friendly and a bit funky, Groovy has diagonals as heavy as its verticals and a c that almost seals shut. But Noto Sans Hanunoo is the plain sans doing the quiet work, with open terminals and a lowercase that fills the height.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Friendly Groovy keeps stems and crossbars at one thickness, with a c that almost closes in a narrow slit. Noto Sans Hebrew takes over below with a dominant midsection and wide gaps at its curve ends, so the heading gets the swagger and the text stays easy to follow.
